title: Kremlin denies Estonian accusation Russia was behind attempted arson that prompted border closure
html:
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov attends a meeting of Russian President Vladimir Putin with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the Grand Kremlin Palace in Moscow, Russia, October 27, 2026. Igor Ivanko/Pool via REUTERS

MOSCOW, Nov 16 - The Kremlin on Monday said it completely denied Estonian accusations that Russia was behind an attempted arson attack that prompted Tallinn to announce it was closing its border with Russia.

Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that all border crossing points with Russia would be closed from December 1, following an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems that Tallinn said had been ordered by Russia's GRU military intelligence service.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the Estonian accusation was part of what he called a pattern of false allegations against Moscow emanating from European countries.

"They are entirely baseless. We therefore cannot accept such accusations. We do not accept them, we do not condone them, we disagree with them, and we completely reject these accusations," said Peskov.

"And, of course, a decision such as this to close all checkpoints and border crossings – well, it’s as if Estonia is building a wall. As history shows, many countries have built walls, which have brought nothing good to those who erected them,” he added. REUTERS
summary: MOSCOW, Nov 16 - The Kremlin on Monday said it completely denied Estonian accusations that Russia was behind an attempted arson attack that prompted Tallinn to announce it was closing its border with Russia.
